subject: Req reprioritization + band exception request
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.example>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.example>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.example>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.example>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.example>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Req reprioritization + band exception request

Team —

Quick ask as we close Q3: recruiting flagged two immediate needs where I think we should reallocate from lower-priority hires to avoid losing a near-offer candidate and to shore up infra capacity for a late-year launch. TL;DR below, details attached.

1) Candidate at risk: Talya Morris (Senior Infra Engineer, interviewing for INF-324). Offer deadline 2026-10-06. Strong fit; market comps show we need to be at ~top-10% of band to be competitive. Recruiting recommends a band uplift for this req or we risk losing the candidate.

2) Req reprioritization: I propose shifting two Q4 junior IC reqs (REQ-728, REQ-731) to 'deferred' and using that budget to cover a one-time band exception and extend the INF-324 offer. This avoids expanding headcount while preserving capacity where it'll matter for the product launch.

Why this matters: INF-324 maps to the customer-facing inference pipeline. Losing the hire delays our KV cache/throughput work and increases risk on the release. The junior roles are less time-sensitive.

Attachments: comp-band-analysis-Q3.xlsx (gap analysis & proposed uplift), candidate-feedback-Talya-Morris.txt (recruiter summary).

Ask: Can HR (Neha) approve a one-time band uplift up to +10% above midpoint for INF-324, and can Finance (Aditya) confirm that moving REQ-728/731 to deferred will free the necessary Q4 spend (no net new headcount)? Recruiting (Priyom) — please hold an offer extension template on standby. Marcus / Lauren — thoughts on product impact if we defer the juniors?

Thanks,

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Engineering, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.example>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.example>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.example>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.example>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.example>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-09-30T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Req reprioritization + band exception request

Sean —

I support prioritizing the infra hire if the candidate is genuinely at risk. Two quick asks before I sign off:

- Aditya: can you confirm the exact Q4 budget delta if REQ-728/731 are deferred? We need the P&L impact and any chargebacks to portfolios.
- Marcus: confirm whether those junior reqs are replaceable from contractor bench for 8–12 weeks (if we defer).

If numbers look clean and Marcus can cover the immediate work, I’m ok with a targeted one-time uplift for INF-324. Neha, if you can outline the approval path (HR committee? VP sign-off?), we can move fast.

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Management
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.example>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.example>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.example>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.example>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.example>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Req reprioritization + band exception request

Quick follow-up after sync with the infra leads. Short answers:

- The two junior reqs (REQ-728 for infra tools, REQ-731 for infra observability) are largely project-based. We can reassign two contractors (existing bench) to cover the next 8–10 weeks without measurable customer impact.
- Expected Q4 spend freed: approx $62k (salary+burden), which covers the one-time uplift plus an offer extension buffer per Sean’s note. Aditya — I’ll forward my line-item estimate in a separate spreadsheet (attached: req-mapping.csv).

Candidate notes I’d add: Talya has deep experience optimizing KV cache and a past infra-to-inference migration. Hiring her reduces known risk on the release path.

If HR signs off on the uplift, recruiting should be authorized to extend the offer.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.example>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.example>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.example>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.example>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.example>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Req reprioritization + band exception request

Thanks everyone — this is the direction I want to take. A couple of operational notes:

- Recruiting: Priyom, please prepare an offer package that includes a one-time sign-on adjustment and a clear band exception rationale. Keep the base within the band cap + up to 10% uplift (per comp-band-analysis attached). Use the extension template but hold on sending until HR confirms.
- Finance: Aditya, confirm the reallocation (Marcus’ $62k estimate) and reply with the formal chargeback note so I can include it in the exec summary.
- HR: Neha, can you escalate this to the compensation committee and confirm the approval path? If possible, a single VP-level approval would be ideal to move quickly.

Forwarding the candidate email below for context.

Date: 2026-10-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Req reprioritization + band exception request

Team —

I reviewed the comp-band analysis and Marcus/Sean’s impact notes. HR approves a one-time, documented band uplift for INF-324 up to +10% above midpoint for this hire only. Conditions:

- The uplift is a one-off exception tied to the candidate and req; it must be recorded in Workday and flagged in the compensation audit trail.
- Recruiting must include an explicit rationale in the offer letter and get candidate acknowledgement on total comp (no later renegotiation allowed).
- Finance (Aditya) will log the offset to REQ-728/731 and confirm the internal chargeback; we need that before we send the offer.

Attachments: approval-note-signed.pdf (HR approval memo).

Neha Kapoor
Head of People Ops
Redwood Inference
